newsitem.title: CONGO: Shots reported near Brazzaville presidency.
newsitem.headline: Shots reported near Brazzaville presidency.

text.p: Shooting broke out on Friday near the presidency in the capital of Congo Brazzaville after a second day of gunfights between supporters of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso and the army, witnesses said.

The shooting began after the start of a second night of curfew in Brazzaville, where the government of Pascal Lissouba has ordered a crackdown on private militias and unauthorised possession of weapons, they added.
The showdown comes ahead of a July 27 presidential election but the significance of the shooting near the presidency was not immediately clear.
One witness spoke of a rocket-propelled grenade or a mortar shell exploding in the grounds of the presidency.
Residents said the national radio and television had stopped broadcasting.

International telephone links with the oil-producing former French colony were down. Contacts were possible via residents plugged into the mobile telephone network in Laurent Kabila Democratic Republic of Congo across the Congo River.

The showdown between Sassou Nguesso and the army follows bloody clashes in the north of the country between supporters of the former president and of Lissouba's campaign manager. The clashes have killed 16 people in less than a month.
Sassou Nguesso has accused Lissouba of trying to foment unrest so as to postpone the elections.

Officals say the army surrounded Sassou Nguesso's home on Thursday as part of efforts to arrest members of his entourage on murder charges stemming from the clashes in the north. The suspects refused to hand themselves in, they added.
